Where the Scrum Master Appears in the Events
Situations and the Scrum Master's Best Action
Scrum Master, Product Owner and Developers Compared
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1The Role in One View

The Scrum Master is one of the three accountabilities of a Scrum Team. The Scrum Guide (2020) describes the role in a few sentences, and almost every exam question about the Scrum Master is built on them.

Item What the Guide says
Where the role sits The Scrum Team consists of one Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers. Within the Scrum Team there are no sub-teams or hierarchies
Accountability 1 Establishing Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide, by helping everyone understand Scrum theory and practice, both within the Scrum Team and in the organization
Accountability 2 The Scrum Team's effectiveness, by enabling the team to improve its practices, within the Scrum framework
Character of the role Scrum Masters are true leaders who serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization
Scrum Definition Scrum "requires a Scrum Master to foster an environment where" the Product Owner orders the work into a Product Backlog, the Scrum Team turns a selection of it into an Increment during a Sprint, the Scrum Team and stakeholders inspect the results and adjust for the next Sprint, and the cycle repeats
Exam angle

the Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum and for the team's effectiveness. The Scrum Master is not accountable for the product's value (the Product Owner), for the Sprint plan or the quality of the work (the Developers), or for a delivery date. When an option makes the Scrum Master decide a product or technical matter, it is almost always wrong.

2The Two Accountabilities

2.1 Establishing Scrum

  • "Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide" means the rules of the framework: the roles, events, artifacts and commitments and the rules that bind them together. The Guide's End Note says the framework is immutable: implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, but the result is not Scrum.
  • The Scrum Master establishes Scrum by helping everyone understand Scrum theory and practice, inside the team and in the organization. Teaching and coaching are the means, not enforcement or policing.
  • Leaving out elements, or not following the rules, "covers up problems and limits the benefits" of Scrum (Guide, Purpose). Part of establishing Scrum is therefore helping people see what a dropped event or a diluted Definition of Done costs them.

2.2 The Scrum Team's effectiveness

  • The Scrum Master enables the Scrum Team to improve its practices. The improvement happens within the Scrum framework: the answer is never to add a role, an event or an artifact that Scrum does not have.
  • Effectiveness is about the team, not the individual: the Scrum Master is not accountable for how much each person produces.
Exam angle

"within the Scrum framework" rules out answers such as adding a project manager, a hardening Sprint or an extra approval meeting. Improve how the team uses the Scrum events and artifacts instead.

3Serving the Scrum Team

The Guide lists four ways. The left column is the Guide's wording. The other two columns are exam-oriented interpretation.

Guide wording What it looks like What it does not mean
Coaching the team members in self-management and cross-functionality Asking questions that help the Developers decide who does what and how; encouraging members to learn skills the team lacks Assigning tasks, deciding for the Developers or being the team's single contact
Helping the team focus on creating high-value Increments that meet the Definition of Done Keeping the Definition of Done and the Sprint Goal in view; helping the team say no to work that would lower quality Inspecting or signing off the quality personally: the Developers instil quality and hold each other accountable
Causing the removal of impediments to the team's progress Making blockers visible and making sure they are resolved, by the team, by the Scrum Master or by others in the organization Fixing every problem alone, or leaving the team to cope with problems it has no authority to solve
Ensuring that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox Making sure each event happens, serves its purpose and ends on time, including teaching the team how Scheduling, running and attending every event personally: the Daily Scrum belongs to the Developers
Exam angle

"causing the removal" and "ensuring" put the Scrum Master in charge of the result, not of doing all the work. A strong answer gets the impediment removed or the event working. A weak answer takes over the work (too controlling) or does nothing (too passive).

4Serving the Product Owner

CSM 3.4 asks for at least three ways the Scrum Master supports the Product Owner. The Guide gives four.

Guide wording Typical example Beyond the Guide
Finding techniques for effective Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management Offering ways to make the Product Goal clear and the Product Backlog ordered, refined and transparent. The Product Owner chooses; the Scrum Master helps
Helping the Scrum Team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items Helping Developers and Product Owner agree what a usable item looks like, so refined items can be Done within a Sprint
Helping establish empirical product planning for a complex environment Planning from what has already happened and adjusting each Sprint. The Guide says forecasting tools such as burn-downs, burn-ups or cumulative flows are useful but "do not replace the importance of empiricism"
Facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed Setting up conversations between the Product Owner and stakeholders and helping the Sprint Review be a working session

What the Scrum Master does not do for the Product Owner: decide the order of the Product Backlog, set the Product Goal or speak for the product. The Product Owner is accountable for these. The Product Owner may delegate the work, but "regardless, the Product Owner remains accountable".

5Serving the Organization

Guide wording What it adds
Leading, training and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption The Scrum Master's role reaches beyond the team: managers, stakeholders and other teams
Planning and advising Scrum implementations within the organization Advising where and how Scrum is introduced, not managing the teams that adopt it
Helping employees and stakeholders understand and enact an empirical approach for complex work Teaching transparency, inspection and adaptation (Topic 01) to people outside the team
Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams Resolving obstacles that keep stakeholders and the team from working together well

The organization-level impediments and the organizational design changes that Scrum brings are covered in Topic 14 (CSM 3.5 to 3.9).

6A True Leader Who Serves

6.1 What the Guide says

"Scrum Masters are true leaders who serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization." Leadership here is exercised through service, influence and example, not through authority over team members: the Scrum Team has no hierarchy, and the Developers are self-managing.

Old wording

The 2017 Guide called the Scrum Master a "servant-leader" for the Scrum Team. The 2020 wording is "true leaders who serve". For exam answers the meaning is the same: the Scrum Master is neither a boss nor an assistant who does what the team or the stakeholders say.

6.2 Scenarios where the Scrum Master leads (CSM 3.1) Beyond the Guide

CSM 3.1 asks for three scenarios. The Guide does not list them, so these are typical examples that follow from its service statements. Any of them can be used on the exam.

Scenario How the Scrum Master leads Guide anchor
Pressure to cut quality to reach a date Models courage and openness, and reminds team and stakeholders that quality does not decrease during the Sprint Sprint rules; Definition of Done; Scrum values
The team is stuck or in conflict Facilitates so that the team reaches its own decision and coaches self-management, instead of deciding for it Coaching in self-management
Improvements stall (the same problems appear each Retrospective) Helps the team pick the most helpful change and act on it as soon as possible The Scrum Team's effectiveness; Sprint Retrospective
Managers or stakeholders interfere with the team Leads the conversation about working through the Product Owner, the Product Backlog and the Sprint Review Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams
The organization adopts Scrum Leads training and coaching and advises on the implementation Serving the organization

7What the Scrum Master Is Not

Exam options often describe the Scrum Master in terms of another role. The Guide's text rules them out.

Misconception What the Guide says
The team's manager who assigns tasks The Scrum Team is self-managing: it decides internally who does what, when and how. There are no hierarchies
The project manager Scrum has three accountabilities and no project manager (CSM 3.9, Topic 14)
The Product Owner's assistant, or the one who orders the Product Backlog The Product Owner orders the items and stays accountable; the Scrum Master helps with techniques
The person who must run every event The Scrum Master ensures events take place. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event
The only person who removes impediments The Scrum Master is accountable for causing the removal; the team and others may do it
The owner of the Definition of Done The Developers are required to conform to it. The Scrum Team creates one if the organization has no standard
Someone who can cancel the Sprint Only the Product Owner has that authority, and only if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete
A required attendee of the Daily Scrum The Scrum Master takes part only as a Developer, if actively working on Sprint Backlog items

8Where the Scrum Master Appears in the Events

Event What the Guide says The Scrum Master's place
The Sprint Fixed length, one month or less; the container for all other events Ensures all events take place and are positive, productive and within the timebox
Sprint Planning The plan is created by "the collaborative work of the entire Scrum Team"; the Product Owner ensures attendees are prepared A member of the Scrum Team who takes part in it
Daily Scrum A 15-minute event for the Developers Not required to attend. If actively working on Sprint Backlog items, takes part as a Developer
Sprint Review The Scrum Team presents results to key stakeholders; a working session A member of the Scrum Team; facilitates stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed
Sprint Retrospective The Scrum Team inspects the last Sprint and plans ways to increase quality and effectiveness A member of the Scrum Team; the team's effectiveness is the Scrum Master's accountability

9Situations and the Scrum Master's Best ActionBeyond the Guide

Exam practice built on the Guide's statements. Use the pattern: serve, coach or facilitate, make it visible, keep Scrum intact, and leave decisions with their owners.

Situation Best action Why
A blocker the team cannot remove itself Make it visible and work with the right people to remove it quickly Causing the removal of impediments; adapt "as soon as possible"
A manager asks who works on what Explain self-management and point to the Sprint Backlog, the Daily Scrum and the Sprint Review The Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work
The Product Owner wants to add work mid-Sprint Help the Product Owner and Developers negotiate scope without endangering the Sprint Goal; new ideas go to the Product Backlog Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner
The team wants to skip the Retrospective Explain what is lost, and help the team see the effects Not operating an event as prescribed loses an opportunity to inspect and adapt
The Product Backlog is vague Help the Product Owner with techniques and help the team see why clear items matter Serving the Product Owner
Stakeholders do not come to the Sprint Review Help the Product Owner and the team engage them Facilitating stakeholder collaboration
The team wants to relax the Definition of Done Remind them that quality does not decrease and unfinished work is not part of the Increment Sprint rules; Definition of Done
Developers disagree on a design Facilitate; the Developers decide How the work gets done is at the Developers' sole discretion
The team asks the Scrum Master to decide who does what Coach the team to decide Coaching in self-management
Other teams want to adopt Scrum Lead, train and coach; plan and advise the implementation Serving the organization

10Scrum Master, Product Owner and Developers Compared

Scrum Master Product Owner Developers
Accountable for Establishing Scrum; the team's effectiveness Maximizing the value of the product; Product Backlog management The Sprint plan; quality through the Definition of Done; daily adaptation; holding each other accountable
Product Backlog Helps with techniques; helps the team value clear items Owns it: develops the Product Goal, creates and orders items, ensures transparency (may delegate) Responsible for sizing the items they will do
Sprint Backlog Not accountable for it Works with the team on the Sprint Goal and on scope during the Sprint Owns it: "a plan by and for the Developers"
Definition of Done Helps the team focus on Increments that meet it The Guide names only the Developers as required to conform to it Required to conform to it
Cancels a Sprint No Yes, the only one No
Daily Scrum Only as a Developer, if working on Sprint Backlog items Same condition The event is for them
How the work is done Coaches and removes impediments Does not decide Decide, at their sole discretion

11Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. Serve and lead; do not command or manage. Reject options where the Scrum Master assigns work, approves work or reports individuals' performance.
  2. Not passive either. "Wait and see" or "let the team figure it out" fails when the team has an impediment it cannot solve or an event that is going wrong.
  3. "Ensure" and "cause" mean accountable for the result. The Scrum Master need not do the work personally.
  4. The Daily Scrum is the Developers' event. The Scrum Master is not required to attend, run it or collect status.
  5. Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and only when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.
  6. Decisions stay with their owners. Product value and order: Product Owner. How to build and the Sprint plan: Developers. The Scrum Master is accountable for Scrum and effectiveness.
  7. Improve within Scrum. Options that add roles, events or artifacts (a project manager, a hardening Sprint, an approval gate) are wrong.
  8. The Scrum Master may work as a Developer on Sprint Backlog items and then takes part in the Daily Scrum as a Developer. The Guide allows it.
  9. Old wording The 2017 Guide spoke of a "Development Team" (now Developers) and made the Scrum Master "responsible for promoting and supporting Scrum", a "servant-leader" who was "facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed" and who taught the Development Team to keep the Daily Scrum within 15 minutes. The 2020 Guide makes the Scrum Master accountable for establishing Scrum, a true leader who serves, who ensures that all events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the timebox. Answer from the 2020 wording.
  10. Absolute words (always, never, only, all) in an option about the Scrum Master are a warning. But check the Guide before rejecting one, because some absolutes are stated rules. Only the Product Owner cancels a Sprint. The Product Owner is one person. Work that does not meet the Definition of Done is not part of the Increment.

12Exam Q&A

12.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1At the Daily Scrum, a Developer reports that the shared test environment has been down for two days and the team has no authority to fix it. What is the best action for the Scrum Master?

  • ATell the Developers to solve it themselves, because the Scrum Master only coaches and never intervenes
  • BWork with the owners of the environment to get it restored quickly
  • CAsk the Product Owner to cancel the Sprint because the plan can no longer be met
  • DRecord the problem and raise it at the next Sprint Retrospective
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Scrum Master is accountable for causing the removal of impediments to the team's progress, which can mean working with others in the organization. Leaving the team alone gives up that accountability, only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint and only when the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, and waiting for the Retrospective delays an adaptation that should be made as soon as possible.

S2A department manager asks the Scrum Master to assign tasks to individual Developers and to send a weekly report on each person's progress. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AAgree, because being accountable for the Scrum Team's effectiveness gives the Scrum Master authority over its members
  • BAssign the tasks but let each Developer choose how to do them
  • CExplain that the Developers decide who does what and point the manager to the Sprint Backlog
  • DAsk the Product Owner to assign the tasks, since the Product Owner orders the work
Show the answer

Answer: C. A Scrum Team is self-managing: it decides internally who does what, when and how, and the Sprint Backlog is a highly visible, real-time picture of the work. The Scrum Master helps the organization understand Scrum rather than build a hierarchy. Assigning tasks, whether by the Scrum Master or by the Product Owner, removes self-management.

S3A new Product Owner keeps the Product Backlog as a long, unordered list of vague requests, and the Developers struggle to plan. How can the Scrum Master best help?

  • AShow the Product Owner techniques for managing the Product Backlog and help the team see why clear items matter
  • BTake over the Product Backlog and order it until the new Product Owner has learned how
  • CTell the Developers to plan from their own ideas until the Product Owner has improved the Product Backlog
  • DAsk the stakeholders to vote on the order of the items so that the Product Owner has less to do
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner by finding techniques for Product Backlog management and by helping the team understand the need for clear and concise items. The Product Owner stays accountable for the content and order of the Product Backlog, so taking it over, bypassing it or handing the order to a vote does not help.

S4Several stakeholders have started giving work directly to individual Developers during the Sprint, and the Sprint Goal is at risk. What is the best action for the Scrum Master?

  • ATell the Developers to follow the stakeholders' requests, because the stakeholders pay for the product and know what they need
  • BCancel the Sprint so that the stakeholders and the Product Owner can agree on what is really needed
  • CForbid any contact between the stakeholders and the Developers for the rest of the Sprint
  • DHelp the stakeholders learn to influence the work through the Product Owner and the Product Backlog
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Product Backlog is the single source of work for the Scrum Team, and those who want it changed convince the Product Owner. The Scrum Master helps stakeholders understand this and removes barriers to collaboration. Following side requests endangers the Sprint Goal, only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and the Scrum Team is expected to collaborate with stakeholders, so a ban is wrong.

S5With two days left in the Sprint, the team proposes counting a Product Backlog item in the Increment although its testing is incomplete, so that the Sprint Review looks better. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AAllow it this once, and ask the Product Owner to add the missing tests to the Product Backlog
  • BRemind the team that work that does not meet the Definition of Done is not part of the Increment
  • CLet the Product Owner decide whether the Definition of Done can be relaxed for this one item, since the Product Owner owns the value
  • DPlan a hardening Sprint after this one so that the testing can be finished
Show the answer

Answer: B. Work cannot be part of an Increment unless it meets the Definition of Done, the Developers are required to conform to it, and an item that does not meet it returns to the Product Backlog. The Scrum Master helps the team focus on Increments that meet the Definition of Done. A hardening Sprint is not part of Scrum, and the Definition of Done is not bent for one item: unfinished work cannot be part of the Increment.

S6Some Developers ask the Scrum Master to attend every Daily Scrum, run it and write down each person's status for the Product Owner. What is the best response?

  • AAgree, because the Scrum Master is accountable for all Scrum events and for what is reported at them
  • BAgree, but only if the Product Owner also attends so that the status can be reviewed
  • CDecline, and tell the team to stop holding the Daily Scrum, because status reports to the Product Owner are unnecessary
  • DExplain that the Daily Scrum is the Developers' event, and make sure it takes place within 15 minutes
Show the answer

Answer: D. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers, who choose their own structure as long as it focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal and produces an actionable plan. The Scrum Master ensures events take place and stay within the timebox, but does not run it as a status meeting. Stopping the event loses a formal chance to inspect and adapt.

S7The head of the department wants the Scrum Team to skip the Sprint Review this time to save a day for development. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AExplain what the Sprint Review is for and what the organization loses if the event is skipped
  • BAgree, and use the saved day for development and an extra Daily Scrum to keep everyone informed
  • CAgree, but ask the Developers to email a summary of the results to the stakeholders instead of meeting
  • DRefuse the request and state that the Scrum Master alone decides which events are held
Show the answer

Answer: A. Each event is a formal opportunity to inspect and adapt, and failure to operate any event as prescribed results in lost opportunities. The Scrum Master helps the organization understand Scrum. An email replaces a working session with a report, and a unilateral refusal ignores the Scrum Master's role of leading by service and influence.

S8The Scrum Master has strong testing skills, and the Developers ask for help with several Sprint Backlog items that are behind. What is appropriate?

  • ADecline, because a Scrum Master must never do any work on the product
  • BHelp, but step down as Scrum Master until the Sprint ends
  • CHelp with the items and, while doing so, take part in the Daily Scrum as a Developer
  • DHelp, but only after the Product Owner has approved it
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Guide says that a Scrum Master actively working on Sprint Backlog items participates in the Daily Scrum as a Developer. Nothing requires the Scrum Master to step down or to obtain approval, and "must never" is an absolute that the Guide does not support.

S9Two Developers disagree about the design of a feature and ask the Scrum Master to make the final decision. What is the best action?

  • ADecide using the Scrum Master's technical experience so that the work can continue
  • BFacilitate a conversation so that the Developers reach their own decision
  • CAsk the Product Owner to choose the design, since the Product Owner is accountable for the product
  • DEscalate to the line manager so that someone with authority makes the decision
Show the answer

Answer: B. How Product Backlog items become Increments is at the sole discretion of the Developers, and the Scrum Master coaches the team in self-management. The Scrum Master and the Product Owner do not decide how the work is done, and escalating to a manager adds a hierarchy that the Scrum Team does not have.

S10After a successful first Sprint, management asks the Scrum Master to help three more teams adopt Scrum. Which response fits the Scrum Master's accountabilities?

  • ADecline, because a Scrum Master serves only the Scrum Team
  • BAccept and take over the management of all four teams
  • CAccept, and help lead, train and coach the organization and advise on the implementation
  • DAsk the first team's Developers to stop their Sprint and train the other teams
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Scrum Master serves the organization by leading, training and coaching it in its Scrum adoption and by planning and advising Scrum implementations. Managing the teams contradicts a design without hierarchy, and stopping a Sprint harms the first team.

12.2 Recall Q&As

R1What are the Scrum Master's two accountabilities?

Show the answer

Establishing Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide (by helping everyone understand Scrum theory and practice) and the Scrum Team's effectiveness (by enabling the team to improve its practices within the Scrum framework).

R2How does the 2020 Scrum Guide describe Scrum Masters?

Show the answer

As true leaders who serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization.

R3In what four ways does the Scrum Master serve the Scrum Team?

Show the answer

Coaching members in self-management and cross-functionality; helping the team focus on high-value Increments that meet the Definition of Done; causing the removal of impediments; ensuring all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the timebox.

R4In what four ways does the Scrum Master serve the Product Owner?

Show the answer

Helping find techniques for Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management; helping the team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items; helping establish empirical product planning for a complex environment; facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed.

R5In what four ways does the Scrum Master serve the organization?

Show the answer

Leading, training and coaching it in Scrum adoption; planning and advising Scrum implementations; helping employees and stakeholders understand and enact an empirical approach for complex work; removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams.

R6How many Scrum Masters does a Scrum Team have?

Show the answer

One. The Scrum Team consists of one Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers.

R7Must the Scrum Master attend the Daily Scrum?

Show the answer

No. It is an event for the Developers. A Scrum Master who is actively working on Sprint Backlog items takes part as a Developer.

R8Who can cancel a Sprint, and when?

Show the answer

Only the Product Owner, if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

R9Who decides how Product Backlog items are turned into Increments?

Show the answer

The Developers, at their sole discretion. No one else tells them how.

R10What does "causing the removal of impediments" imply?

Show the answer

The Scrum Master is accountable for getting impediments removed. The Scrum Master, the team or others in the organization may do the actual work.

R11Which phrase replaced "servant-leader" in the Guide?

Show the answer

"True leaders who serve." The 2017 Guide used servant-leader.

R12What does "ensuring that all Scrum events take place" cover?

Show the answer

That the events happen, that they are positive and productive, and that they stay within the timebox.

R13Which Guide statement shows that the Scrum Master is not the team's manager?

Show the answer

Within a Scrum Team there are no sub-teams or hierarchies, and the team decides internally who does what, when and how.

R14What does the Product Owner keep if the work of Product Backlog management is delegated?

Show the answer

Accountability. The Product Owner may delegate the work, but remains accountable.

13Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Accountabilities Establishing Scrum · the Scrum Team's effectiveness
Character True leader who serves (old wording: servant-leader)
Serves the team Coach self-management and cross-functionality · focus on Increments that meet the Definition of Done · cause removal of impediments · ensure events take place, are positive, productive and timeboxed
Serves the Product Owner Techniques for Product Goal and Product Backlog · clear, concise items · empirical product planning · facilitate stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed
Serves the organization Lead, train, coach adoption · plan and advise implementations · empirical approach for stakeholders · remove barriers
Team shape One Scrum Master, one Product Owner, Developers; no sub-teams or hierarchies
Daily Scrum Developers' event; Scrum Master joins only as a Developer if working on Sprint Backlog items
Cancel a Sprint Product Owner only (Sprint Goal obsolete)
Decisions Value and order: Product Owner · how and the Sprint plan: Developers · Scrum and effectiveness: Scrum Master
Best-answer pattern Serve, coach or facilitate · make it visible · keep Scrum intact · leave decisions with their owners · act, do not wait
Wrong-answer pattern Command or assign · decide for the team · add roles or events · do nothing · "never" and "always"
